brief: A note-taking app in 3D space — recent notes float near, old ones drift away, connections are threads

dominant_strengths: Atmospheric navy palette with subtle blue glow threads creates a believable depth metaphor and quiet, contemplative mood
Concept of distance-as-recency is poetic and differentiates from linear note apps; the faded top-left card hints at this clearly
Card typography hierarchy (title, body, timestamp) is consistent and legible at the foreground depth
dominant_weaknesses: Overlapping cards at the same z-plane collide and render text as unreadable double-exposure (top-left Research/Concept stack)
Connection threads are barely visible and inconsistent — the core metaphor of 'glowing threads between thoughts' is underdelivered
Floating toolbar (+, undo, record) feels generic and detached from the spatial language; no z-depth cues or contextual affordance
fix_priorities: Resolve card collision: enforce minimum spatial separation or fade/blur stacked cards by depth instead of overlapping opacity
Strengthen thread connections — make them visible primary citizens, with curvature, glow intensity tied to relationship strength
Add parallax/scale cues so depth reads instantly; current cards are nearly the same size, flattening the 3D promise
Redesign the toolbar to match the spatial idiom (orbital controls, depth slider) rather than flat 2D chrome
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral mood is strong and reflective metaphor is intriguing, but behavioral usability collapses where overlapping cards become unreadable.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the depth-and-decay concept is legible, but the 'threads' and true 3D drift are too timid to fully realize the brief.
